hook: Vahdat leads engineering strategy for Google's AI infrastructure as Chief Technologist for AI Infrastructure, a role created in December 2025 after fifteen years at the company building its Tensor Processing Unit chips, data center networking, and compute systems. He previously served as Vice President and General Manager of Machine Learning, Systems and Cloud AI.

standing.watch: What the records leave open is mostly the shape of the new role. The Chief Technologist for AI Infrastructure position was announced in December 2025, and the site records no further detail about its scope, its reporting line or what it changes relative to his previous job running Machine Learning, Systems and Cloud AI. The Tensor Processing Unit program and the data center networking work remain the substance of his record, and how they are organized under the new title is not stated. The one case the site tracks, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, is filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded, and it does not name him or his companies, so nothing in the records ties its outcome to him. On these records there is no pending listing, no announced dispute and no dated next step for Vahdat himself.
standing.record: The site's records on Vahdat are narrow and institutional. Two companies appear, Google and Google Cloud, and he is listed as an executive of each. His background is documented through credentials rather than deals: a PhD in computer science from UC Berkeley in 1998, the SAIC endowed chair in computer science and engineering at UC San Diego before he joined Google in 2010, a Google Fellow designation in 2015 and induction into the National Academy of Engineering in 2023. The only lawsuit on the site is Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded by this tracker, and that case names Anthropic rather than Vahdat or either of his companies. The pattern across these records is a career spent inside one employer on infrastructure, with no litigation of his own and no outside ventures recorded.
standing.standing: Amin Vahdat stands at the center of Google's compute buildout as Chief Technologist for AI Infrastructure, a role the records say was created in December 2025 after fifteen years at the company. He leads engineering strategy for Google's AI infrastructure, which places him over the systems that train and serve models rather than over a product line. Before the new title he was Vice President and General Manager of Machine Learning, Systems and Cloud AI, overseeing the Tensor Processing Unit chip program. The site lists him as an executive of both Google and Google Cloud, so his influence runs through the parent company and its cloud arm at once. His standing rests on hardware and networking, the Tensor Processing Unit chips, data center networking and compute systems he spent his tenure building.
